sights.n: Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall
sights.w: Wan Qing Yuan, the 1880s villa off Balestier Road that Dr Sun Yat Sen used as his Southeast Asian base for the Tongmenghui — now a National Monument whose galleries tell how overseas Chinese communities bankrolled and shaped the 1911 Revolution. Anchor stop on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail.

sights.n: Maha Sasana Ramsi Burmese Buddhist Temple
sights.w: Singapore's Burmese Buddhist temple, founded on Kinta Road in 1878 and rebuilt beside the Sun Yat Sen villa on Tai Gin Road in 1991 — it houses the largest white-marble Buddha outside Myanmar, carved from a single block of Mandalay marble. On the 'Faith, Film and Food' route of NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail.

sights.n: Goh Chor Tua Pek Kong Temple & Wayang Stage
sights.w: Balestier's red temple, founded in 1847 by Hokkien labourers on Joseph Balestier's sugar-cane estate ('Goh Chor' = Rochore), rebuilt in southern Chinese style in 1920/1928 — and beside it one of Singapore's last permanent wayang (Chinese opera) stages, built 1906 by Tan Boo Liat and still used by troupes during the Hungry Ghost Festival. Conserved by URA.
sights.k: Temple + 1906 opera stage; performances in the 7th lunar month

sights.w: The sole surviving rural-market building in Singapore, designed by local architect Kwan Yow Luen with animal-and-flower reliefs across its cream walls — a heritage-trail stop that still trades as a cluster of eateries. A planned April 2025 closure was reversed — the tenancy was extended by two years (Seth Lui, Feb 2025).

sights.address: Balestier Road, Singapore (to confirm at geocode)
sights.w: An 18-storey 1986 apartment block whose stacked, Lego-like cubic modules — each home with its own terrace — were inspired by Moshe Safdie's Habitat 67 in Montreal: Balestier's modernist landmark, seen from the street.
sights.k: Modernist residential landmark — view from outside

sights.w: The 1973 hawker centre and wet market spread across HDB blocks 90, 91 and 92 on Whampoa Drive — successor to the old Rayman Market and a stop on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail. Two cooked-food halls side by side hold some of Balestier's best breakfasts: Hoover rojak, fish-head bee hoon, lor mee, Hokkien mee.
sights.k: Hawker centre & wet market; most stalls morning to mid-afternoon

sights.n: Former Malay Film Productions Studio (Shaw Studio)
sights.w: Shaw Brothers' Malay Film Productions studio on Jalan Ampas (1947-1969), where more than 150 films — many starring P. Ramlee — were shot in the golden age of Malay cinema. The surviving studio gate and buildings sit at the end of a quiet lane off Balestier Road.
sights.k: Heritage site — exterior only; on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail

sights.w: A 1950s row built over former taro farmland and ponds, unusual for shophouses in housing a separate apartment on each floor — streamlined Art Deco façades conserved with the pre-war shophouses along Balestier Road in 2003.
sights.k: Conserved streetscape — view from Balestier Road

sights.address: Ah Hood Road / Jalan Rajah, Balestier, Singapore
sights.w: A small green with an open lawn and pond, named for Dr Sun Yat Sen (Sun Zhongshan) — it faces the villa where he stayed, now the Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall.
